rows.what the ink shows: A long descending p begins the word, followed by a compact rounded join and a short r shoulder; there is no tall initial d or closing c sequence.
The struck word between système and entier has a tall initial t, a low rounded ou connection, and a second rising t at the right. The cancellation crosses the low joins without hiding both t stems.

Faint upper traces above the darker replacement are crossed by a narrow horizontal stroke; the small letter bodies and any circumflex cannot be separated sufficiently to certify the deleted word or its exact layer allocation.

The darker word has an open c, compressed on joins leading to a crossed t, an i dot, and the low ment run ending in a hooked t. A short raised angled mark lies over the middle vowel, but the inspected view does not distinguish both arms of a circumflex; that accented component remains uncertain.

A heavy horizontal cancellation runs through the entire proposed phrase. Small upper bumps and an upright at the left-middle survive, with a large hooked descending stroke at the right, but the separate bodies of pris, comme, and un are not recoverable.

The opening parenthesis is clear and securely belongs to this cancelled phrase. The following word has a loop rising above the strike and two short uprights; the next has a tall double upright, but the heavy line covers its interior and prevents distinguishing the two complete candidate word sequences.

The following group begins with a descending p-like stem and a rounded upper turn. Its remaining low letters are covered by a thickened part of the cancellation, so the whole word pour is not established.

On the next line the cancelled span retains a small initial peak, scattered low joins, and a later upright. The broad horizontal stroke merges the intervening bodies and obscures divisions; the source illegible count of two is retained without independent verification.

Following the end of non nulles, a rounded fragment and a descending stroke survive among the large diagonal cancellation loops. The internal h/a/q/u sequence of chaque is interrupted too heavily to certify the full word.

The intervening area has isolated short upright and low horizontal remnants under several long diagonal and looping cancellation strokes. Neither complete word bodies nor their divisions are separable; the source illegible count of two is retained without independent verification.

In the later part of this line a downward stroke meets a long barred baseline, while diagonal cancellation loops cross the following low joins. The p-like onset alone does not establish the covered our body.

At the next line start a small trough-shaped letter and angular upright remnants survive, but the large cancellation loops cut through the proposed membership sign and parenthesized L(E) group. Each symbol cannot be distinguished independently, so the formula remains uncertain.

Small curved parenthetical pieces and low index-like strokes remain on the deleted formula line, but large diagonal cancellation loops intersect the baseline lambda, inner wedge and raised-letter position. The complete letters and index/superscript cannot be separated from those loops.

A small rounded rho bowl with a long descender and a right closing curve survive. A thick curved deletion runs through the lower right of rho where the proposed i lies, and the left parenthesis is intersected by the diagonal deletion, so the complete indexed parenthesis remains uncertain.

At the end of the deleted block, low humps and a short downward remnant survive along the bottom rule. The rule covers the oval and joins needed to distinguish both proposed words; on a cannot be recovered completely.

The expanded extent shows a left upright, a lambda-like sign with a low short 1, a second lambda-like sign farther right, and a terminal upright. The intervening marks and second index are covered by the cancellation, and the first upright cannot securely be allocated to the preceding le; the initial bare lambda_1 is withdrawn and the source span is retained wholly uncertain.

The correction region contains two short overwritten lines at the far right and further inserted writing below the canceled baseline. Looped initials and joined low strokes survive, but the complete words formule and ci-contre cannot both be allocated independently of the neighboring premier-member text.

The deleted group before the surviving absolute-value bar has an angular descending stroke and a separate dark low cluster. Multiple heavy oblique and horizontal strokes cross both, preventing an independent reading of lambda and its proposed lower 1.

There is an initial low connected stroke, a detached dot and a deep descending hooked stroke followed by two small rising strokes. They support an abbreviated or compressed maj sequence, but the following strokes and the exact terminal punctuation do not distinguish the complete proposed maj. securely.
An upright stem at left and a rounded right-hand loop remain in the small deleted group. An angular overstroke merges the intervening marks, so the d/apostrophe/o division cannot be certified.

The raised 1, slash and 2 are visible, as is a small raised star between two crossed baseline positions; the wedge/n and both baseline factors are heavily overwritten. One closing curve lies before the raised fraction and a larger curve after it, leaving the proposed full base and exponent scope uncertain.

Below hermitien positif, a descending initial and short connecting humps are followed by a taller stroke and a detached dot. The horizontal cancellation and oblique loop merge the letters of the first word and the joins of the second, so both complete words remain uncertain.

rows.what the ink shows: The initial variable/et positions are cut by the long rule; a later op.-like bowl and stop, the descender within the compacts position, and low final word strokes survive below it. The rule merges essential joins in several separate words, so the entire proposed phrase is retained uncertain.

In the rotated marginal sentence, the word has a long low e/s entry, a distinct descending p with returning shoulder, then the compact a/c/e joining stroke before the separated de. These surviving strokes support espace.

The deleted group after Hilbert has a high initial loop, a lower descending stroke and an ending hook, but two thick horizontal strokes join and cover the internal letter bodies. Neither the whole sequence complexe nor an alternative can be certified from those remnants.

The deletion before pour les notations contains an initial round remnant and a pronounced downstroke beneath the cancellation line. The thick line covers the remaining bodies, so the proposed two words on pose stay uncertain.

After voir, a short rising-and-level group is followed by a longer word with a looped middle, a crossed upright and a separate dot. These support parts of la rédaction, but the low initial letter sequence and the accent cannot be separated confidently from the close red rule and surrounding ink.

The word after une has low joined initial curves, a long downstroke in its middle and a flattened trailing sequence. The short internal curves and acute accent are insufficiently distinct to certify every letter of conséquence.

The following word shows low joined humps, a taller middle stroke and detached dots, but its middle and final strokes meet perpendicular ink from the main text. The full sequence immédiate, including its accent, remains uncertain.

The group after le has an open c followed by the compressed joined arr strokes and a raised acute above the final e. A separate tall d and shallow u follow before premier, supporting both words carré du.

The symbol following the equals sign has a closed upper loop and a long descending stem, unlike the forked lambda at the start of the preceding line. A separate small stroke sits at its lower right as the index 1.

The parenthetical group before Voir has descending p-like strokes and a small rounded middle, but the last small stroke and any period are crowded against the following capital and cancellation. I cannot securely isolate the numeral 2 or the complete abbreviation.

After Voir, several parallel cancellation strokes cover low connected remnants; a descender and isolated rounded parts remain between the bars. They do not establish complete words or reliable word divisions; the original two-word illegible count is retained but remains unverified.

A clear opening parenthesis immediately follows the squared norm and securely begins this marked note. A tall f-like stroke then leads into a partly joined word, with more than one rounded or stem-like component at the right; neither facteurs nor a lone rho is secure, and the later span boundaries remain unresolved.

The next slanted line contains separated upright and low connected strokes, with an apparent dot or accent above one group. I cannot isolate a reliable h followed by two parallel equals bars, nor securely assign a replacement word to this source span.

At the end of the slanted note, short connected remnants and taller intersecting strokes remain, including a parenthesis-like curve near the end. Their word division and full sequence are unresolved; the existing two-word count is retained but remains unverified.
